newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - Utility demand supports heavy grades.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - Utility demand supports heavy grades.

text.p: Asia's heavy crude prices on Friday remained strong on healthy utility demand from Japan.
An August parcel of Duri was sold by an equity producer to a shosha at ICP +1.01 per barrel, for direct burning use in Japan.
Although demand for Duri from fuel oil blenders was now limited due to the rising premiums, demand from utilities was expected to keep prices supported.
July Minas was also sold to a Japanese refiner at ICP +48, firmer than the last July trades done around ICP +25/30.
Most of the July Minas cargoes had already been committed, but sellers squeezed additional barrels to meet the good demand.
An end July/early August Labuan was heard sold at OSP even, with an end August Tapis said done to Japan also at OSP even.
But there was thin discussion for the other August light crudes, with only NWS condensate offered a few cents premium over the NWS APPI quotes.
Bangchak's crude purchase tender has still not been fully concluded, with some financial details still to be agreed.
"We should know by tonight" said the European major supplying the crude to Bangchak.
The tender awarded 800,000 barrels of August Murban.
The level was heard at Dubai +85, although the seller said that "it was slightly lower than that".
Oman prices became more bearish on widespread talk that a major had bought an Oman cargo at MPM -10, the lowest level seen for some time.
Some traders were uncertain of the trade, considering the level too low.
August Oman traded around Dubai +3 earlier in the month.
